product.title: Despre imunitate
product.description: În această carte îndrăzneaţă şi fascinantă, Eula Biss abordează problema fricii noastre faţă de guvern, faţă de sistemul medical şi faţă de ceea ce se poate afla în aerul, alimentele, saltelele, medicamentele şi vaccinurile copiilor noştri. Reflectând asupra propriei experienţe de tânără mamă, Biss ne sugerează că nu ne putem imuniza copiii şi nu ne putem imuniza nici pe noi înşine împotriva lumii. Pe măsură ce explorează metaforele care înconjoară subiectul imunităţii, Biss îşi extinde conversaţiile cu alte mame la meditaţii asupra mitului lui Ahile, asupra lui Candide de Voltaire, a lui Dracula de Bram Stoker şi a altor opere literare şi nu numai. Despre imunitate este un vaccin împotriva fricii noastre şi o povestire emoţionantă despre cum suntem cu toţii interconectaţi – cu corpul nostru şi cu soarta noastră.Eula Biss este autoarea cărţilor The Balloonists şi Notes from No Man’s Land, care a câştigat National Book Critics Circle Award pentru critică. Scrierile ei au apărut în The Believer, Harper’s Magazine şi The New York Times. A fost beneficiara unor burse de cercetare de la Guggenheim Foundation, Howard Foundation şi National Endowment for the Arts. Locuieşte la Chicago şi predă la Northwestern University.„... incredibil de bine scrisă.“Bill Gates„Despre imunitate... se foloseşte de metaforă şi mit, de ştiinţă şi sociologie, de filosofie şi de politică pentru a ţese o tapiserie bogată în introspecţie şi inteligenţă.“The New York Review of Books„Este un comentariu intelectual la cel mai înalt nivel, o cercetare a celor mai profunde probleme privind sănătatea, identitatea şi tensiunile între deciziile individuale ale părinţilor şi cele impuse de societate.“The Washington Post

# About Immunity: Navigating Fear, Science, and Connection

Are we truly immune? Eula Bissâs powerful non-fiction book, *About Immunity*, offers a fascinating, deeply reflective examination of our collective anxieties surrounding health, science, and the modern world. Far beyond a purely scientific text, this literary work delves into what it means to be connectedâto our bodies, our history, and each other.

If you are seeking a nuanced discussion that blends intellectual rigor with emotional depth, this book is essential reading for anyone grappling with complex issues of societal trust and personal health decisions.

## A Literary Exploration of Immunity

In *About Immunity*, Eula Biss tackles the palpable anxieties surrounding public healthâfrom vaccines and medicine to what we breathe in the air or consume in our food. Using her own experience as a young mother, Biss challenges us to question the narratives built around immunity. She suggests that neither we nor our children can be truly immunized against life's complexities; rather, true protection lies in understanding the myths and systems that surround us.

The book is notable for its unique approach, weaving together disparate intellectual threads:
*   **Mythology and Literature:** Biss expands her conversation beyond science, drawing parallels to literary works like Voltaireâs *Candide*, Stoker's *Dracula*, and even the ancient myth of Achilles.
*   **Interconnectedness:** It is described as an emotional story about how interconnected we all areânot just physically, but in our fate and collective experiences.
*   **Critical Analysis:** The work functions as a powerful commentary on the tension between individual parental choices and the demands of society.

## Why This Book Resonates with Readers

The critical reception highlights *About Immunity* not merely as general health advice, but as an advanced piece of intellectual writing. Critics praise its ability to weave together complex subjects:

> "Using metaphor and myth, science and sociology, philosophy and politics to weave a rich tapestry of introspection and intelligence."
> â The New York Review of Books

This is described by *The Washington Post* as "an intellectual commentary at the highest level" and an investigation into deep issues concerning health, identity, and societal pressures.

## Meet the Author: Eula Biss

Eula Biss is a highly acclaimed writer whose work has appeared in prestigious publications such as *The Believer*, *Harperâs Magazine*, and *The New York Times*. She is the author of *The Balloonists* and *Notes from No Man's Land*, earning recognition including the National Book Critics Circle Award for criticism. Biss continues to contribute her insightful writings while residing in Chicago, where she teaches at Northwestern University.

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Q: Is this book purely scientific?**
A: No. While it addresses serious scientific topics like immunity and vaccines, the core of *About Immunity* is literary, philosophical, and sociological. It uses science as a starting point for a broader discussion on human fear and connection.

**Q: Who should read this book?**
A: Anyone interested in non-fiction that blends deep thought with narrative structureâespecially those who enjoy reading about the intersection of health policy, philosophy, and modern parenting struggles.
